history.alt_text: An electric vehicle powering specific glowing windows of a dark house via a heavy-duty charging cable during a blackout.
history.caption: Sizing for an outage means powering critical loads, not the whole house.
history.title: EV-V2H-Critical-Loads-Backup

style_when: the article describes one decisive moment or place — a yard at dawn, a control room, a shutdown line, a handover — that a film still could hold
prompt: Cinematic film still, anamorphic 35mm look, wide establishing composition. An unbranded modern electric vehicle parked in a suburban residential driveway at deep blue-hour twilight during a total neighborhood power outage. The vehicle is connected to the dark house by a heavy-duty, glowing illuminated charging umbilical cable. Only two ground-floor windows of the house glow with warm amber practical light, illustrating isolated critical loads, while the surrounding houses and streetlights remain pitch black. Crisp atmospheric depth, restrained teal-and-amber palette, dramatic deep shadows, no people facing camera, realistic driveway textures.
negative_prompt: text, words, letters, numbers, watermarks, UI, generic stock, people
rationale: The story is about home energy resilience during an outage and the critical loads required. A cinematic still of a modern EV acting as a backup power source (V2H) illuminating only the critical rooms of a house during a neighborhood blackout perfectly captures the tension of targeted backup power against widespread outage.
cue: A home battery should be sized against the critical loads
subject: An unbranded modern electric vehicle powering a dark suburban home through an illuminated heavy-duty charging cable
core_thesis: A home battery should be sized against the critical loads it has to carry for the length of the outage, not the household's annual utility bill.
core_conflict: Sizing against massive whole-house daily consumption vs. the actual small footprint of critical backup circuits.
composition: wide establishing atmospheric frame, asymmetrical subject placement on the lower thirds
